Then Mu'awiyah was enraged,
and he sent Abu'l-A'war with an army.
And when they came to the place which is called Phoenix,
they found Emperor Constans and his brother Theodosius there.
And when they prepared to do battle on the following day,
Emperor Constans slept,
and he saw in his dream that he was in Thessalonica.
And when he related it to an interpreter of dreams, he answered him:
"Would that,
O Emperor,
you had not slept,
and had not seen this dream!
For 'Thessalonica' is interpreted:

'Give the victory to another!'"
And when the emperor made light of the interpretation of the dream, he drew up the battle of the ships in the midst of the sea;
and the Romans were defeated.
And the emperor himself would also have been killed,
had not the son of Bucinator leaped into the imperial ship,
and transferred the emperor to another ship so that he might be saved.
And he himself remained in the imperial ship,
and killed many,
and was also killed.
And Constans and his brother fled {OCR?} to the royal city (Constantinople).
And about twenty thousand corpses of the Romans were found floating upon the water.
And when the Arabs prepared again to go up against Constantinople,
Ptolemy came out and gave gold,
and made peace for three years.
Now Constans killed his brother Theodosius,
and on this account he was hated by his armies.
And he was afraid and went to Rome.
And when he tarried, the armies mutinied against him, saying:
"It is not fitting for the emperor to be in Rome,
because it is far from the Arabs."
Then he came to the island of Sicily.
And when he reached Syracuse,
it pleased him to dwell there.
And he sent after his sons;
the citizens would not consent, saying:
"We will not let our emperors depart from our midst."
Then he made his three sons autocrats:
Constantine, Tiberius, and Heraclius;
and he settled them in the royal city,
while he dwelt in Syracuse,
because he was afraid of his armies lest they kill him,
for they used to call him 'a second Cain'.
